result.title: How to Explain your Unexplainable Video Anomaly Detector
result.comment: This paper has been accepted at the RWS workshop WACV 2027
result.summary: Weakly-supervised Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) models assign anomaly scores from high-dimensional features, and their predictions remain unexplained. Saliency maps show where a model looks but not what it relies on, and the descriptions produced by Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are generated by branches that the anomaly score never reads. To address this faithfulness gap, we propose \textbf{Explain The Unexplainable (ETU)}, a classifier-agnostic framework that audits frozen VAD models through counterfactual interventions in their feature space. ETU maps video features to a discrete dependency graph of agents, actions and outcomes ($A_r \to A_a \to A_o$), regenerates the features by graph-conditioned diffusion with selected nodes of the graph masked, and measures the change in the score of a frozen detector; one set of interventions is applied unchanged to every detector. The generator is trained only to reconstruct the input features, so it cannot learn the contrast it is asked to measure, and we validate the audit with experiments that test every alternative explanation of its results, from the cost of regeneration to random deletions of matched size. On UCF-Crime features obtained from a CLIP encoder, we show that substituting the scene semantics results in the largest drop for most detectors, and that removing the outcome chain of the graph ($Δ_{rel}$) changes the anomaly score of all six audited detectors far more than removing the same number of random nodes, even though the random deletion perturbs the features about as much. We show that this targeted behavior comes from the divergence objective of the graph embedding. Without it, the two interventions become indistinguishable, and with a divergence objective in the generator as well, the score change of the detector follows the displacement of the reconstruction rather than the semantics that were removed.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ETU，一个与分类器无关的审计框架：将视频特征映射为「主体→动作→结果」的离散依赖图，在图条件扩散重建特征时遮蔽选定节点，再用冻结 VAD 检测器异常分数的变化衡量各语义节点的忠实贡献，并以随机删除等对照实验排除替代解释。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结模型＋latent 特征空间反事实干预＋同规模随机删除对照」的因果检验程序，可能可供核查 LVR 中答案是否真正依赖被遮蔽的视觉证据与特定语义节点，并为 latent 状态的贡献分配提供可迁移的测量线索；但研究对象是视频异常打分而非多模态推理，迁移可行性有待阅读正文评估。
